namespace_decision.taken_under: the owner's explicit blanket approval for this lane
namespace_decision.statement: ZooKeeper concepts extracted from kafka/chap02.md are rooted at `kafka.zookeeper.*`, not at a standalone `zookeeper.*` root.
evidence: L8 — 브로커의 메타 데이터를 저장하기 위해 사용되는 아파치 주키퍼: the chapter introduces ZooKeeper only as the store for Kafka broker metadata.
L10-L13 — ZooKeeper support is being dropped in recent Apache Kafka versions and replaced by KRaft; the source frames ZooKeeper's very lifetime by Kafka's roadmap.
L208-L224 — the only connection contract given is `zookeeper.connect`, a Kafka broker parameter.
The chapter carries no technology-agnostic ZooKeeper claim: no ZooKeeper API, no non-Kafka client, no coordination use case outside Kafka.
namespace_decision.non_move_consequence: Both `concept_id` and `canonical_path` derive from this root, so it cannot be changed after apply without moving every ZooKeeper document. Should a later source supply technology-agnostic ZooKeeper evidence, the correct response is a new `zookeeper.*` concept relating to these, not a rename of these eight; `apply` refuses to move an approved concept (`batch proposal may not move an approved concept`), so a rename would need an explicit migration lane.
namespace_decision.messaging_root_rationale: Batch 05 contains no technology-agnostic messaging evidence, so the batch-04 rule (`messaging.*` only for genuinely technology-agnostic messaging concepts with direct evidence) yields no `messaging.*` concept.

id_rules.N0: concept_id = kafka.<area>.<slug>, area derived from the governing H2 heading: 주키퍼 → zookeeper, 카프카 설치 → install, 브로커 설정 → config, 하드웨어 선택 → hardware.
id_rules.N0b: The pre-heading preamble L7-L16 has no governing H2 (heading_chain = `unheaded-body`). Its one candidate, KRaft, is filed under `kafka.zookeeper.*` because the evidence defines KRaft solely as ZooKeeper's replacement, keeping the deprecation pair co-located.
id_rules.N1: For a configuration parameter, slug = the parameter name exactly as the source writes it, lowercased, `.` → `-`.
id_rules.N1b: Refinement recorded here: ZooKeeper's parameters are camelCase, not dotted. Applying N1 literally would yield `ticktime`/`initlimit`/`clientport`. Batch 05 does not mint per-parameter ids for them at all — they are grouped into `kafka.zookeeper.timing-parameter` and `kafka.zookeeper.ensemble-port` under N2 and carried as aliases, so N1 is applied unchanged to all 16 dotted Kafka parameters and never stretched.
id_rules.N2: For a non-parameter concept, slug = kebab-case of the established English term.
id_rules.N3: canonical_path = content/brain/knowledge/kafka/<area>/<leaf>.md where leaf = slug, except when slug === area, in which case leaf = kafka-<slug> (folder_route rule). Applied here to kafka.zookeeper.zookeeper → kafka/zookeeper/kafka-zookeeper.md.
id_rules.N4: tags[] equals the canonical_path folder segments; `brain`/`knowledge` reserved. The raw frontmatter display tag `📚 카프카 핵심가이드` (L5) is never copied.
id_rules.alias_policy: knowledge_aliases are search-only (policy H-1). No `aliases`, `alias` or `permalink` routing key is emitted. Under the repaired exact-alias search contract an exact alias match claims rank 0, so every batch-05 title and alias was checked for an EXACT normalized match against the 384 applied title-or-alias identities (119 titles + 265 aliases) and against every other batch-05 identity.

candidates.title: 핵심 브로커 매개변수
candidates.concept_granularity: single set of broker settings that may stay at defaults on a standalone broker but must be changed to run in cluster mode

candidates.title: broker.id
candidates.concept_granularity: single integer broker identifier that must be unique within a cluster and pinned per host

candidates.title: listeners
candidates.concept_granularity: single listener list binding protocol, hostname and port for the connections a broker accepts

candidates.title: zookeeper.connect
candidates.concept_granularity: single connection string locating the ZooKeeper holding broker metadata, optionally under a chroot path

candidates.title: log.dirs
candidates.concept_granularity: single list of local log directories, with new partitions placed by partition count rather than by used disk space

candidates.title: num.recovery.threads.per.data.dir
candidates.concept_granularity: single per-log-directory thread count governing how fast log segments open, check and close around broker restarts

candidates.title: auto.create.topics.enable
candidates.concept_granularity: single switch deciding whether a broker creates a missing topic on produce, consume or metadata request

candidates.title: auto.leader.rebalance.enable
candidates.concept_granularity: single background rebalancer that keeps partition leadership spread evenly across brokers

candidates.title: delete.topic.enable
candidates.concept_granularity: single switch that blocks arbitrary topic deletion in a cluster

candidates.title: 파티션
candidates.concept_granularity: single append-only log within a topic that guarantees order inside itself, provides redundancy and horizontal scale, and whose per-topic count is the unit of load distribution, consumer parallelism and retention

candidates.title: 토픽별 기본값
candidates.concept_granularity: single broker-level default set applied to newly created topics, overridable only through the admin tooling

candidates.title: num.partitions
candidates.concept_granularity: single default partition count for auto-created topics, increasable but never decreasable afterwards

candidates.title: default.replication.factor
candidates.concept_granularity: single default replication factor for auto-created topics, recommended to exceed min.insync.replicas by at least one

candidates.title: 내고장성
candidates.concept_granularity: single platform property of continuing correct operation while individual components fail, sized in Kafka by holding the replication factor above the minimum in-sync replica count

candidates.title: RF++
candidates.concept_granularity: single replication sizing rule setting the replication factor two above min.insync.replicas, i.e. at least three replicas per partition

candidates.title: log.retention.ms
candidates.concept_granularity: single time-based retention setting evaluated against each closed log segment's last-modified time, with the smallest declared unit winning

candidates.title: 메세지 보존
candidates.concept_granularity: single durability rule holding messages for a configured time or partition size before expiry, evaluated per partition against closed log segments

candidates.title: log.retention.bytes
candidates.concept_granularity: single size-based retention setting applied per partition, so retained volume scales with partition count

candidates.title: log.segment.bytes
candidates.concept_granularity: single segment size threshold that closes and rolls a log segment, gating expiry and timestamp-to-offset lookup

candidates.title: log.roll.ms
candidates.concept_granularity: single time threshold that closes a log segment independently of its size, at the cost of synchronized closes

candidates.title: min.insync.replicas
candidates.concept_granularity: single minimum count of in-sync replicas that must acknowledge a write before it is reported successful

candidates.title: message.max.bytes
candidates.concept_granularity: single broker-side ceiling on compressed message size that must stay aligned with the consumer and replica fetch sizes

candidates.title: 카프카 하드웨어 선택
candidates.concept_granularity: single provisioning frame listing the five hardware dimensions that bound broker performance and partition capacity

candidates.title: 디스크 처리량
candidates.concept_granularity: single broker disk-write property that bounds producer acknowledgement latency and drives the SSD-versus-HDD choice

candidates.title: 디스크 용량
candidates.concept_granularity: single storage sizing derived from retained traffic plus overhead, and one of the two factors that size a cluster

candidates.title: 페이지 캐시
candidates.concept_granularity: single system memory region serving tail reads from cached log segments instead of from disk

candidates.title: 브로커 힙 메모리
candidates.concept_granularity: single modest JVM heap requirement for a Kafka broker, leaving the rest of system memory to the page cache

candidates.title: 네트워크 대역폭
candidates.concept_granularity: single bandwidth budget that bounds cluster traffic and is skewed outbound by fan-out consumers, replication and mirroring
